gap: No result ChatGPT got states what any star & ocean projector draws or costs to run: the one with a published power rating, Govee's app- and Matter-controlled Star Light Projector (Ocean Wave) H6094, is rated 10 W, so 8 hours a night for a year costs at most about $5.30 at the August 2026 US average residential rate of 18.16¢/kWh. On cost per effect, the 24-film '5D' listings work out to $1.25–$1.92 per film and the Govee to $1.75 per built-in scene.
standout_why: I compared against the pages ChatGPT got: the Glarex, Retrowave and Sientle product pages, the Walmart '5D Holographic' listings (cited #3, plus #4–#8 and #12) and the bestproductsreviews.com roundups. None of the snippets or listing titles gives wattage, running cost, coverage per dollar or price per film; the titles only give film counts. I couldn't open some pages: Walmart showed a bot check, glarexx.com returned HTTP 429, sientle.com and retrowave.online failed on certificate errors, and the bestproductsreviews.com page came back empty. The cited YouTube video page loaded without its title or description. I also read two blogs from outside the results. Device Diary's Topacme 5D review (Sam, June 28, 2026) gives coverage in a 12 × 12 ft room but no wattage. ibisik.com's Comauo piece (Juliet, Aug 30, 2026) says only that it is 'USB-powered'.
decides: This supports making the Govee H6094 the 'smart' pick over the generic '5D holographic' listings. It is the only candidate with a maker's US product page that names its controls (Govee Home app, Alexa, Google Assistant, Matter), its power (10 W, 5 V 2 A) and its coverage (540 ft², $0.13 per ft²). A year of nightly use costs about $5, so running cost can't decide the pick. The generic 24-film listings are cheaper per film ($1.25–$1.92) than the Govee is per scene ($1.75), but those are physical slides and the Govee's are built-in digital scenes, so the gap isn't a real saving. The generic listings publish no wattage and no app details, so their 'smart' claim can't be checked.
